texts.preamble: Shri Ram Niwas Dhuria vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi on 3 November, 2022 In The Court Of Shri Anuj Agrawal Additional Sessions Judge-05, South East District, Saket Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 205 of 2022 Cnr No. Dlse01-009836-2022 Shri Ram Niwas Dhuria R/o House No. 3488, Gali No. 81, Block -E-2, Molar Band Extension New Delhi-110044. . . . . Appellant Versus 1. The State of Nct of Delhi 2. Sh. Kanti Prasad Upadhyay S/o Sh. Leela Dhar R/o H. No. 265, Gali No. 12, Block-F, Molar Band Extension, New Delhi-110044. . . . . Respondent Instituted on : 27.10.2022 Reserved on : Not Reserved Pronounced on : 03.11.2022 Judgment
texts.facts: 3. The appellant has raised number of grounds impugning the judgment dated 17.08.2022. The complainant can challenge the order of acquittal by filing an application for special leave to appeal in the Delhi High Court and not in the Sessions Court. ... ... ..." It was a complaint case under Section 7 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, in which Subhash Chand was tried and he was acquitted by the learned Metropolitan Magistrate. The State filed criminal appeal before the Sessions Court under Section 378(1) (a) CrPC. Preliminary objection regarding maintainability of the appeal before the Sessions Court was rejected. That order was challenged before this Court (Delhi High Court) and it was held that Sessions Court had no jurisdiction to entertain the appeal. He cannot file such appeal in the Sessions Court.
texts.arguments: For the sake of convenience, the provisions of section 378 (4) Cr.P.C are being reproduced which reads as under: "378. Appeal in case of acquittal (1)......... (2)......... (3)......... (4) If such an order of acquittal is passed in any case instituted upon complaint and the High Court, on an application made to it by the complainant in this behalf, grants special leave to appeal from the order of acquittal, the complainant may present such an appeal to the High Court" 5. I am fortified in my view by dicta of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subhash Chand Vs State (Delhi Administration), 2013 (1) JCC 338, wherein the Hon'ble CA No. 205/22 Ram Niwas Dhuria vs. State & Anr. Supreme Court in para no.s 17 and 21 held as under:- "17. 6. Further, Hon'ble Delhi High Court in a recent judgment of "The Bhajanpura Cooperative Urban Thrift & Credit Society Ltd. Vs. Sushil Kumar", Crl. Appeal No. 972/2014, decided on 3.9.2014, at CA No. 205/22 Ram Niwas Dhuria vs. State & Anr. The controversy now is no longer res integra in view of the pronouncement of law by Supreme Court in 'Subhash Chand Vs. State (Delhi Administration)', (2013) 2 SCC 17. The Supreme Court further observed: "Thus, whether a case is a case CA No. 205/22 Ram Niwas Dhuria vs. State & Anr. Section 378 (4) places no restriction on the complainant... ... ..." 16. In a recent case 'Bhavuben Dineshbhai Makwana Vs. State of Gujarat & Others', 2013 Crl LJ 4225, Full Bench of Gujarat High Court answering the reference on question number (3) 'If the victim prefers an appeal before this Court, challenging the acquittal, invoking his right under proviso to section 372 of CrPC, whether that appellant is required to first seek leave of the Court, as is required in case of appeal being preferred by the State?', held: 'If the victim also happens to be the complainant and the appeal is against acquittal, he is required to take leave as provided in Section 378 of the Criminal Procedure Code but if he is not the complainant, he is not required to apply for Shri Ram Niwas Dhuria vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi on 3 November, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19470126/ 5 or obtain any leave. For the appeal against inadequacy of compensation or punishment on a lesser offence, no leave is necessary at the instance of a victim, whether he is the complainant or not.' 17. Kerala High Court has also in 'Omana Jose Vs. State of Kerala', ILR 2014 (2) Kerala 669 decided on 11.4.2014 on reference of Criminal Revision Petitions in the light of conflicting decisions in 'Sree Gokulam Chit and Finance Co. (P) Ltd. & Another Vs. T. Krishnakumar & Others', 2013 (4) KLT 547 (supra) and 'Shibu Joseph & Others Vs. Tomy K.J. & Others', ILR 2013 (4) Ker. 866, concluded: "For the aforesaid reasons, we hold that the complainant in a case under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act cannot challenge the order of acquittal before the Sessions Court under the proviso to Section 372 of the CrPC and his remedy is only to file an appeal to the High Court with special leave under Section 378 (4) CrPC." 18. In the CA No. 205/22 Ram Niwas Dhuria vs. State & Anr.
